Mathlib/Order/SuccPred/Basic.lean and Mathlib/Order/Interval/Set/SuccPred.lean prove the
same six statements, under different names:

statement Order/SuccPred/Basic.lean (ns Order) ctx Order/Interval/Set/SuccPred.lean (ns Set) ctx
Ici (succ a) = Ioi a Ici_succ{,_of_not_isMax} Preorder Ici_succ_eq_Ioi{,_of_not_isMax} LinearOrder
Icc (succ a) b = Ioc a b Icc_succ_left{,_of_not_isMax} Preorder Icc_succ_left_eq_Ioc{,_of_not_isMax} LinearOrder
Ico (succ a) b = Ioo a b Ico_succ_left{,_of_not_isMax} Preorder Ico_succ_left_eq_Ioo LinearOrder
Iio (succ a) = Iic a Iio_succ{,_of_not_isMax} LinearOrder Iio_succ_eq_Iic{,_of_not_isMax} LinearOrder
Ico a (succ b) = Icc a b Ico_succ_right{,_of_not_isMax} LinearOrder Ico_succ_right_eq_Icc{,_of_not_isMax} LinearOrder
Ioo a (succ b) = Ioc a b Ioo_succ_right{,_of_not_isMax} LinearOrder Ioo_succ_right_eq_Ioc{,_of_not_isMax} LinearOrder

I figure that half of these need deprecating, but I struggle with deciding which ones. The ones in SuccPred/Basic.lean are earlier in the import hierarchy, so if one wants to avoid downstream breakages, we should keep those (while porting the better names, plus the hypothesis-free form of Ico_succ_left_eq_Ioo from Interval/Set/SuccPred.lean). But that would break the explicit symmetry that Interval/Set/SuccPred.lean has with its sibling Interval/Finset/SuccPred.lean, which I also find unsightly.

I see @Yaël Dillies is the sole author of both files, so tagging you for your advice specifically.

As an aside, I notice that Ici_succ_eq_Ioi*, Icc_succ_left_eq_Ioc* and Ico_succ_left_eq_Ioo can be generalized from LinearOrder to Preorder for free.
The SuccPred.Basic ones are the ones I meant to deprecate (name-wise, at least)
I agree on the names. Do you also have an opinion on where the surviving statements should live?
So Interval/Set/SuccPred.lean, then. Mind if I draft a PR for this?
A PR covering the required generalizations needed before we can replace the lemmas in Basic.lean: https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/pull/43519
